title: Arkansas Inbred Eggs

ingredients.item: slices of sandwich bread (1/2–3/4 inch thick)

steps: Use a round cutter (shot glass or similar) to cut a circle in the center of each bread slice. Reserve the circle “cut-out.”
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Melt 2 Tbsp butter, swirl to coat.
Place both bread slices in the skillet (buttered side down), along with the cut-out circles. Toast until golden (about 2-3 minutes).
Flip bread slices. Crack an egg into each hole in the bread. Season egg + bread lightly with salt & pepper.
Cook until egg whites are mostly set (about 3-4 minutes). If you like, cover pan to help cook the top of the egg gently.
Once yolks are to your liking, flip carefully for a few seconds to finish the other side (optional). Remove and serve with the reserved cut-outs.
notes:
Use a moderately thick bread so it holds the egg without collapsing. The cut-out can be toasted too, good for dipping yolk. If you like runny yolks, keep the heat medium and cover the pan for part of cooking.

Nutrition: Serving 1 egg in bread · Calories 200 · Fat 14g · Saturated fat 6g · Unsaturated fat 8g · Trans fat 0g · Cholesterol 210mg · Sodium 150mg · Carbs 15g · Fiber 1g · Sugar 2g · Protein 9g

not_healthy: 4 Tbsp butter adds a lot of saturated fat.
White sandwich bread is refined carbs.
